intro: Long ago, builders made giant stone churches by hand. They used tools like the square, the level and the plumb line. Young helpers learned from skilled builders. The builders met in a hut called a lodge.

Later, many clubs took the name lodge. Members paid a little money so they could help each other. They helped sick workers, widows and children. Some lodges built hospitals. Chicago had a very tall lodge building.
In this unit, you will name a builder's tools. You will tell how clubs helped families. You will also learn what a kind club does when you ask it questions.
bigQuestion: How did builders and helpers make their towns stronger?

timeline.t: Builders start Notre-Dame, a big stone church in Paris.
Builders start Cologne Cathedral in Germany. It takes more than 600 years.
Someone writes a rule book in verse for builders in England.
A paper in Scotland lists questions to test the Mason Word.
The Odd Fellows start a lodge in Baltimore to help members.
A Prince Hall lodge meets in Chicago.
Chicago's tall Masonic Temple is finished.
Mooseheart, a town for children, opens in Illinois.
The first Shriners hospital for children opens in Louisiana.
A Shriners hospital for children opens in Chicago.

title: Builders and Helpers

chapters.title: The Stone Builders
chapters.bigQuestion: How did builders long ago make giant stone churches by hand?

story.title: Tom Signs His First Stone
story.kicker: A young builder finishes his very first stone. How will everyone know it is his?
paragraphs: Long ago, in England, a boy named Tom works at a big church. The church is not done yet. Men lift stones with ropes. Hammers go tap, tap, tap. Tom is learning to be a builder. (Tom is made up, but boys like him were real.)

Tom holds a small iron chisel and a wooden mallet. For many days, he has cut one block of stone. He makes each side flat. He makes each corner square. His teacher, Master John, checks it with a tool shaped like an L.
"Good work," says Master John. "Now sign it." Tom smiles. He cannot write his name yet. But he has his own mark. It looks like a little arrow. He carves the arrow on the side of the stone.
The stone goes up into the wall. Many years later, people still see Tom's arrow there. It says, "A young builder made this with care." Tom feels proud. He is part of something big.
story.think: If you had your own mark to carve on your work, what would it look like? Why would you pick that shape?

lessons.title: Churches Made of Stone
lessons.mainIdea: Long ago, stonemasons built big churches and castles out of stone.
reading: Look at a huge old church in France or England. Its walls are made of stone. Its windows reach up high. People built it about 800 years ago.
The builders were stonemasons. A *stonemason* cuts stone and builds with it. They built churches, castles, bridges and walls.
A very big church is called a *cathedral*. Some cathedrals are as tall as a tower. Many of them still stand today.

words.d: a worker who cuts stone and builds with it
a very big, important church

look.title: A Castle on a Hill
look.text: Look at the gray castle on the hill. Its walls are thick stone. Each stone is a big block. The blocks fit close together, like toy bricks. A tall tower stands at one corner.
look.prompt: Who do you think cut and stacked all these stones? Point to the part that would be hardest to build.

check.q: What is a stonemason?
choices: A worker who cuts stone and builds with it
check.why: A stonemason cuts stone and builds with it.

check.q: What is a very big, important church called?
check.why: The reading says a very big church is called a cathedral.

check.q: Which of these did stonemasons build?
check.why: Stonemasons built churches, castles, bridges and walls.

lessons.title: Built by Hand, Year by Year
lessons.mainIdea: Big stone churches took many years to build, all by hand.
reading: Long ago, there were no big machines. No trucks. No motors. Workers cut every stone by hand. They lifted stones with ropes and wheels.
That took a long, long time. A worker might help build a church his whole life. His children might finish it after him.
A church in Cologne, Germany, was started in 1248. It was not done until 1880. That is more than 600 years!

words.d: made by people using their hands and tools, not big machines

look.title: How Long to Build?
look.cite: Encyclopaedia Britannica, articles on Salisbury Cathedral (1220-1258), Notre-Dame de Paris (1163-c. 1260) and Cologne Cathedral (1248-1880)
look.prompt: Which church took the longest to build? Which one was the fastest?

check.q: How did workers long ago cut stone?
check.why: There were no big machines. Workers cut every stone by hand.

check.q: Which church took more than 600 years to finish?
check.why: Cologne Cathedral was started in 1248 and done in 1880.

check.q: Why could children finish a church their parents started?
choices: Building took a very long time
check.why: Big stone churches took many years. Some took longer than one life.

lessons.title: The Square and the Level
lessons.mainIdea: A square checks corners, and a level checks that a stone is flat.
reading: Master John picks up a tool shaped like the letter L. It is called a *square*. He holds it on the corner of a stone. If the corner fits the L, it is just right.
Another tool is a *level*. It shows if the top of a stone is flat. A flat stone does not tip or slide.
Why check? If one stone is crooked, the next stone sits crooked too. Good checking keeps a whole wall strong.

words.d: a tool shaped like an L that checks a corner
a tool that shows if something is flat

look.title: Stack the Blocks
look.text: Look at two stacks of toy blocks on the table. In the first stack, every block sits flat. It is tall and steady. In the second stack, the bottom block is tipped. The whole stack leans to one side.
look.prompt: Which stack will fall first? Which tool would a builder use to fix the bottom block?

check.q: Which tool is shaped like the letter L?
check.why: A square is shaped like an L. It checks corners.

check.q: What does a level show?
check.why: A level shows if the top of a stone is flat.

check.q: Why did builders check each stone?
choices: So the wall would be strong
check.why: One crooked stone makes the next one crooked. Checking keeps the wall strong.

lessons.title: The Plumb Line and the Mallet
lessons.mainIdea: A plumb line checks that a wall stands straight up, and a mallet taps the chisel.
reading: Tie a heavy weight to a string. Hold the string up high. The weight pulls the string straight down. This is a *plumb line*.
Builders held a plumb line next to a wall. If the wall matched the string, it stood straight up. If not, it leaned.
To shape stone, a builder held a sharp chisel. He tapped it with a wooden hammer called a *mallet*. Tap, tap. Little chips fell off.

words.d: a string with a weight that hangs straight down
a wooden hammer used to tap a chisel

look.title: Make a Plumb Line
look.text: Look at the string in your teacher's hand. A big metal washer is tied to the end. The washer hangs still. The string is straight up and down. Your teacher holds it next to the classroom door.
look.prompt: Does the side of the door match the string? Try it with a string and a washer at home or in class.

check.q: What is a plumb line?
choices: A string with a weight that hangs straight down
A tool shaped like an L
check.why: A plumb line is a string with a weight. The weight pulls it straight down.

check.q: What did a builder tap with a mallet?
check.why: The builder tapped a sharp chisel with the mallet to shape stone.

check.q: What does a plumb line help a builder check?
choices: If a wall stands straight up
check.why: If the wall matches the string, it stands straight up.

lessons.title: An Apprentice Learns
lessons.mainIdea: An apprentice learned a trade by working next to a skilled master for years.
reading: Tom did not go to a school to learn building. He worked next to Master John every day. He watched. He tried. He tried again.
Tom was an *apprentice*. An apprentice learns a job by working with a skilled person. Learning often took about seven years.
At first, Tom swept and carried. Later, he cut small stones. At last, he could cut big stones well. Then he was a trained builder.

words.d: a person who learns a job by working with a skilled worker
a job that takes special skill, like building with stone

look.title: Learning Step by Step
look.text: Look at three pictures in a row. In the first, a boy sweeps stone dust. In the second, he cuts a small stone while his teacher watches. In the third, he cuts a big, smooth block all by himself.
look.prompt: What is one thing you learned step by step, like riding a bike? Who helped you?

check.q: What is an apprentice?
choices: A person who learns a job by working with a skilled worker
A king who owns a castle
check.why: An apprentice learns a job by working with a skilled person.

check.q: About how long did learning often take?
check.why: The reading says learning often took about seven years.

check.q: What did Tom do first as an apprentice?
check.why: At first, Tom swept and carried. Later he cut stones.

lessons.title: A Mark on the Stone
lessons.mainIdea: Many builders carved their own small mark on stones they cut.
reading: Look closely at an old stone church. On some stones, you may see tiny carved shapes. One looks like an arrow. One looks like a star.
Each one is a *mason's mark*. Each builder had his own mark. He carved it on stones he cut.
Why? Many experts think the marks showed who cut each stone. Then the boss could check the work and pay the right builder.

words.d: a small shape a builder carved on a stone he cut

look.title: Marks on a Wall
look.text: Look at an old stone wall. On one block is a small arrow. On another is a shape like a letter X. On a third is a little star. The same arrow shows up on five more stones.
look.prompt: How many builders do you think cut these stones? Draw a mark you could use on your own work.

check.q: What is a mason's mark?
choices: A small shape a builder carved on his stone
check.why: A mason's mark is a small shape a builder carved on a stone he cut.

check.q: What was Tom's mark in the story?
check.why: In the story, Tom's mark looks like a little arrow.

check.q: Why do many experts think builders used marks?
choices: To show who cut each stone
check.why: The marks helped show who cut each stone, so the right builder was paid.

sections.title: The Lodge at the Building Site

lessons.title: A Hut Called a Lodge
lessons.mainIdea: Builders met in a hut at the building site called a lodge.
reading: Next to the church, the builders had a small wooden hut. They kept their tools there. They ate lunch there. They cut stone there on rainy days.
This hut was called a *lodge*. The builders who worked together were a team. They met in the lodge to plan and to learn.
Builders also had rules. An old rule book from about 1390 still exists. It told builders to work hard and be fair.

words.d: a hut at a building site where builders met and worked
something a group agrees everyone should do

look.title: An Old Rule Book for Builders
look.text: Do honest work every day. Be fair about pay. Keep your master's plans to yourself. Be polite at church and at the table.
look.cite: The Regius Poem, a rule book for masons written in verse, about 1390 (British Library, Royal MS 17 A I)
look.prompt: Which rule would help a team of builders the most? Which rule could your class use?

check.q: What was the builders' hut called?
check.why: The hut at the building site was called a lodge.

check.q: What did builders do in the lodge?
check.why: The builders kept tools, ate lunch and cut stone in the lodge.

check.q: What did the old rule book tell builders?
check.why: The rule book from about 1390 told builders to work hard and be fair.

lessons.title: Only Trained Builders
lessons.mainIdea: Builders kept their methods to themselves so only trained people did the work.
reading: Cutting stone is hard. A bad cut can make a wall fall. So builders taught their methods only to apprentices. They did not tell just anyone.
In Scotland, trained builders had a *password* called the Mason Word. A new builder said it to show he had learned the trade.
A password like that is a safe secret. It keeps work safe. But a secret about someone getting hurt is not safe. Always tell a trusted grown-up.

words.d: a secret word that shows you belong
an adult who listens to you and helps keep you safe

look.title: Questions for a New Builder
look.text: A paper from Scotland lists questions that masons asked a man who said he knew the Mason Word. If he answered well, they knew he was trained.
look.cite: Edinburgh Register House Manuscript, 1696 (National Records of Scotland)
look.prompt: Why would builders want to know a new worker was really trained?

check.q: Why did builders teach their methods only to apprentices?
choices: So only trained people did the hard work
check.why: A bad cut can make a wall fall. Only trained builders should do the work.

check.q: What was the Mason Word?
check.why: In Scotland, trained builders had a password called the Mason Word.

check.q: A secret is about someone getting hurt. What do you do?
check.why: A secret about someone getting hurt is not safe. Always tell a trusted grown-up.

review.q: What do we call a worker who cuts stone and builds with it?
review.why: A stonemason cuts stone and builds with it.

review.q: Which tool checks that a wall stands straight up?
review.why: A plumb line hangs straight down. A straight wall matches it.

review.q: What is a very big, important church called?
review.why: A cathedral is a very big, important church.

review.q: Tom carved a little arrow on his stone. What was it?
review.why: Each builder had his own mason's mark. Tom's was an arrow.

review.q: Where did builders keep their tools and eat lunch?
review.why: The lodge was a hut at the building site for tools, lunch and work.

review.q: How did Tom learn to be a builder?
choices: He read a book in one day
He worked next to a master for years
review.why: Tom was an apprentice. He learned by working with Master John.

chapters.title: Lodges That Help
chapters.bigQuestion: How can a club help its members and its neighbors?

story.title: Help Comes to the Door
story.kicker: Papa is too sick to work. Who will help the family now?
paragraphs: Long ago, about 120 years ago, Rosa lives in Chicago. Her family has a small home on a busy street. Papa works hard every day. But one winter, Papa gets very sick. He has to stay in bed. (Rosa is made up, but families like hers were real.)
Mama looks worried. With no work, there is no pay. How will they buy food? How will they pay the doctor? Rosa sits by the window and watches the snow.
Then someone knocks. It is Mr. Cole from Papa's lodge. Papa is a member of this club. Mr. Cole brings money from the lodge. He says, "We help each other. The lodge doctor will come tomorrow."
Each week, the lodge brings help until Papa is well. When spring comes, Papa goes back to work. He tells Rosa, "Now I will help the next family." Rosa smiles. That is what good neighbors do.
story.think: How did the lodge help Rosa's family? Who helps your family when things are hard?

lessons.title: From Builders to Clubs
lessons.mainIdea: Later, many clubs called lodges formed so members could help each other.
reading: Remember the builders' hut called a lodge? Later, the word *lodge* came to mean a club, too. Many members were not builders at all.
Some lodge clubs are the Freemasons, the Odd Fellows and the Moose. Members met in a lodge room. They became friends.
A big idea for many lodges was helping. Each *member* paid a little money. When a member needed help, the lodge used that money.

words.d: a club, or the room where its members meet
a person who belongs to a club or group

look.title: A Jar for Helping
look.text: Look at the big glass jar on the lodge table. Each member drops in one coin every week. The jar fills up slowly. One day, a member cannot work. The lodge takes coins from the jar to help him.
look.prompt: Why is it good that everyone puts in a little? What could your class save up for together?

check.q: What did the word lodge come to mean later?
choices: A club, or the room where it meets
check.why: Later, the word lodge came to mean a club and its meeting room.

check.q: What is a member?
choices: A person who belongs to a club
check.why: A member is a person who belongs to a club or group.

check.q: How did many lodges save money to help?
check.why: Each member paid a little money. The lodge used it when a member needed help.

lessons.title: Help When Someone Is Sick
lessons.mainIdea: Many lodges paid for doctors and gave money when a member was too sick to work.
reading: Long ago, a sick worker got no pay. His family could go hungry. That was scary for many families.
Many lodges had a *lodge doctor*. The doctor visited sick members. The lodge helped pay the cost.
Many lodges also gave sick members money each week. That is what Mr. Cole brought to Rosa's family. It helped until Papa was well.

words.d: a doctor who cared for the members of a lodge

look.title: The Doctor's Visit
look.text: Look at the doctor at the door. He holds a black bag. He smiles at Rosa. He walks to Papa's bed and listens to his heart. Mama does not have to pay him today. The lodge will help.
look.prompt: How do you think Rosa feels when the doctor comes? Why?

check.q: Why was it hard when a worker got sick long ago?
choices: He had to build a church
check.why: Long ago, a sick worker got no pay, and his family could go hungry.

check.q: Who is a lodge doctor?
choices: A doctor who cared for lodge members
check.why: A lodge doctor visited and cared for the members of a lodge.

check.q: What did Mr. Cole bring to Rosa's family?
check.why: Mr. Cole brought money from the lodge to help while Papa was sick.

lessons.title: Help for Widows and Children
lessons.mainIdea: Many lodges helped widows and children when a member died.
reading: Sometimes a member died. His wife was then a *widow*. She had to care for the children alone. Many lodges helped her with money.
Lodges also helped pay for the funeral. A funeral is a time when people gather to say goodbye.
Some lodges helped children whose mom or dad had died. The Moose club built a whole town for children in Illinois. It is called Mooseheart. It opened in 1913.

words.d: a woman whose husband has died
a time when people gather to say goodbye to someone who died

look.title: A Town for Children
look.text: Look at the town on the farm near Batavia, Illinois. There are homes, a school and a big green field. Children walk to class together. Grown-ups there help care for them. The Moose club members pay to keep it going.
look.prompt: What would a child need in a town like this? Name three things.

check.q: What is a widow?
choices: A woman whose husband has died
check.why: A widow is a woman whose husband has died.

check.q: Which club built Mooseheart, a town for children?
check.why: The Moose club built Mooseheart in Illinois. It opened in 1913.

check.q: What is a funeral?
choices: A time to say goodbye to someone who died
check.why: A funeral is a time when people gather to say goodbye.

lessons.title: People Helping People
lessons.mainIdea: Many different groups started their own lodges so their families could get help too.
reading: Long ago, some lodges would not let everyone join. Black families were often kept out. Many Catholic families had their own rules about joining.
So people started their own lodges. Black Americans built Prince Hall lodges. Chicago had one by 1852. Catholic men started the *Knights of Columbus* in 1882.
These lodges helped widows, sick members and neighbors, too. People helping people made whole neighborhoods stronger.

words.d: a club for Catholic men, started in 1882, that helps families
a person who lives near you

look.title: When Some Lodges Began
look.cite: Independent Order of Odd Fellows history; Most Worshipful Prince Hall Grand Lodge of Illinois history; Knights of Columbus history
look.prompt: Which of these began first? Which began last?

check.q: Why did some people start their own lodges?
choices: Some lodges would not let them join
check.why: Some lodges kept people out. So they started their own lodges.

check.q: Which club did Catholic men start in 1882?
check.why: Catholic men started the Knights of Columbus in 1882.

check.q: When did Chicago have a Prince Hall lodge?
check.why: The reading says Chicago had a Prince Hall lodge by 1852.

lessons.title: The Shriners Build Hospitals
lessons.mainIdea: A club called the Shriners built hospitals to care for children.
reading: The *Shriners* are a club. Freemasons started the Shriners club. Shriners often wear a red hat called a fez in parades.
About 100 years ago, the Shriners wanted to help children. They built a *hospital* just for children. The first one opened in 1922, in Shreveport, Louisiana.
Children came to get help with bones and walking. Children got care even if their families could not pay.

words.d: a club, started by Freemasons, known for building children's hospitals
a place where doctors and nurses care for people who are sick or hurt

look.title: A Parade With Red Hats
look.text: Look at the parade on the street. A group of men walk by. Each wears a small red hat with a black tassel. Some drive tiny cars. A sign they carry says they help children's hospitals.
look.prompt: What club is this? What does the sign tell you about what they do?

check.q: What did the Shriners build?
check.why: The Shriners built hospitals to care for children.

check.q: Where did the first Shriners hospital open in 1922?
check.why: The first Shriners hospital opened in Shreveport, Louisiana, in 1922.

check.q: What is a hospital?
choices: A place where doctors care for sick or hurt people
A hut at a building site
check.why: A hospital is where doctors and nurses care for people who are sick or hurt.

lessons.title: A Hospital in Chicago
lessons.mainIdea: In 1926, the Shriners opened a children's hospital in Chicago.
reading: The Shriners in Chicago met in a big building called Medinah Temple. They wanted a hospital in their city, too.
In 1926, they opened a Shriners hospital in Chicago. It was the 11th Shriners hospital. It helped many children walk and play.
Chicago still has a Shriners hospital for children today. Nurses, doctors and helpers work there every day.

words.d: a person trained to care for people who are sick or hurt

look.title: The Chicago Hospital Opens
look.text: The Shriners hospital in Chicago opened on March 20, 1926. It was the 11th Shriners hospital. Shriners from Medinah Temple helped build it.
look.cite: Shriners Children's Chicago, Our History (hospital website)
look.prompt: What year did the Chicago hospital open? Who helped build it?

check.q: When did the Shriners open a hospital in Chicago?
check.why: The Chicago Shriners hospital opened in 1926.

check.q: Where did the Chicago Shriners meet?
check.why: The Chicago Shriners met in a big building called Medinah Temple.

check.q: Which Shriners hospital was the Chicago one?
check.why: The Chicago hospital was the 11th Shriners hospital.

lessons.title: A Very Tall Temple
lessons.mainIdea: In 1892, Chicago's Masonic Temple was one of the tallest buildings in the world.
reading: In 1892, a new building went up in Chicago. It stood at State Street and Randolph Street. It was called the *Masonic Temple*.
It had more than 20 floors. That was very tall long ago! It was one of the tallest buildings in the world. Shops were at the bottom. Lodge rooms were at the top.
The building is gone now. It was torn down in 1939. But people still remember it in old pictures.

words.d: a tall Chicago building from 1892 with lodge rooms at the top
one level of a building; also called a story

look.title: How Many Floors?
look.cite: The Skyscraper Museum, Tallest Towers: Masonic Temple; Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat
look.prompt: Which building has the most floors? How many more floors did the Masonic Temple have than the Home Insurance Building?

check.q: What year was Chicago's Masonic Temple built?
check.why: The Masonic Temple went up in Chicago in 1892.

check.q: What was at the top of the Masonic Temple?
check.why: Shops were at the bottom. Lodge rooms were at the top.

check.q: What happened to the Masonic Temple in 1939?
check.why: The building was torn down in 1939.

lessons.title: Kind Clubs Welcome Questions
lessons.mainIdea: A kind club is happy to answer your questions about what it does.
reading: Ava wants to join a club. She asks, "What do you do?" The leader smiles. "We help at the food bank," she says. "Ask us anything."
A kind club likes every *question* you ask. It tells you what it does. It is happy for your family to know, too.
A club may have a fun password. That is fine. But no one should ask you to hide something that hurts. Tell a trusted grown-up.

words.d: something you ask to find out more
an adult who listens to you and helps keep you safe

look.title: Two Clubs
look.text: Look at two clubs. The first club says, "We clean the park. Bring your mom or dad to see!" The second club says, "Don't tell your family about us. It is a secret."
look.prompt: Which club acts like a kind club? What would you do if a club said the second thing?

check.why: A kind club likes questions and tells you what it does.

check.q: Someone says, "Hide this from your family. It hurts." What do you do?
check.why: No one should ask you to hide something that hurts. Tell a trusted grown-up.

check.why: The leader said her club helps at the food bank.

review.q: What did the Shriners build for children?
